claim_text: Thames Valley Police arrested Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor on February 19, 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office and released him under investigation.
Former DP World chief Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem became executive chairman of Malaysia's MMC Port Holdings in July 2026, prompting 31 civil-society groups to urge that the appointment be revoked.
The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as U.S. Attorney General on August 8, 2026 by a 50-49 vote.
A Bloomberg analysis published July 24, 2026 found Epstein's staff booked more than 3,700 commercial flights between 2009 and 2019, with no identifiable passenger in more than 1,700 records.
A federal judge gave final approval on August 27, 2026 to Bank of America's $72.5 million class settlement with Epstein accusers.
President Trump removed Pam Bondi as U.S. Attorney General on April 2, 2026, and Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche became acting attorney general.

Brazil's Federal Public Prosecutor's Office opened a confidential procedure on February 10, 2026 to examine whether Brazilian women were recruited for Jeffrey Epstein; no public result had been reported as of September 24, 2026.
Six women sued Epstein's estate and co-executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn in New York state court on August 19, 2026 under New York City's Gender-Motivated Violence Act.

By May 2026 Swedish MP Gustaf Göthberg had been appointed a Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe rapporteur to examine Epstein's network and its links to former Secretary General Thorbjorn Jagland.

DOJ filed a notice of appeal of Judge Sullivan's September 16, 2026 order on September 17 and on September 22 asked the D.C. Circuit (No. 26-5299) to stay the foreign-language-records portions of the June 25 and September 16 orders and to expedite the appeal.

At the July 2, 2026 injunction deadline in Phang v. Blanche, DOJ declined to produce additional unredacted records, defended its redactions, and asked the court for 60 more days or to accept its reasons.

Reuters and CNN reported DOJ sent lawmakers a summary covering over 300 officials and politically exposed persons in Epstein-related records, while stating inclusion in that summary does not itself establish wrongdoing.
The DOJ Office of the Inspector General announced in April 2026 an audit of DOJ compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
Reuters reported DOJ sent lawmakers a Feb. 15, 2026 letter describing redaction rationale and stating four newly discussed individuals were not directly tied to wrongdoing in reviewed records.
Reps. Massie and Khanna said on September 18, 2026 that the discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act II had reached 218 signatures.
AP reported file excerpts described Epstein referencing Nobel committee leadership in outreach messages to high-profile contacts.

Two women filed a proposed class action against Epstein's estate in the Southern District of New York in mid-September 2026 on behalf of people pictured in his seized collection of child sexual abuse material, seeking at least $6 million and a notification program.

The Washington Post reported on September 9, 2026 that investigators in Poland, Norway, and Latvia said DOJ had not answered their mutual legal assistance requests; DOJ said it had not refused any jurisdiction.

On August 18, 2026 Magistrate Judge Ryon McCabe recommended that survivors' Federal Tort Claims Act negligence suit against the FBI, seeking about $320 million, proceed to 90 days of limited discovery.
Seven women sued hairstylist Frederic Fekkai in New York state court on September 1, 2026 over his salon's alleged role in grooming young women for Epstein; Fekkai denies the allegations.

On July 23, 2026, 156 Harvard affiliates published an open letter calling for an independent investigation of Harvard's Epstein ties and consequences for people who legitimized Epstein after his 2008 conviction.

The Harvard Crimson reported on May 1, 2026 that Harvard Medical School gave Epstein a $75 million active donor rating in July 2012 and that Harvard mailed him personalized endowment updates from 2009 through 2018, items not discussed in Harvard's 2020 review.
The House voted on September 16, 2026 to hold Leon Black in contempt of Congress for defying House Oversight subpoenas in its Epstein investigation.
The Council of Europe waived Thorbjorn Jagland's immunity on February 11, 2026, and Okokrim charged him with aggravated corruption on February 12, 2026; he denies the charges.

Digital Garage announced in late February 2026 that Joi Ito would retire as senior managing executive officer on March 31 and leave its board at the June shareholders' meeting, citing a scheduled term expiration.
Norway's Okokrim charged diplomat Mona Juul with aggravated corruption and her husband Terje Rod-Larsen with complicity in aggravated corruption on February 9, 2026.
Dean Kamen resigned from the FIRST board of directors on March 12, 2026; FIRST's board chair said its independent review found no evidence of misconduct.
King Charles III's lawyers declined Rep. Ro Khanna's request that the king meet Epstein survivors during his April 2026 U.S. state visit, citing an ongoing investigation.
Epstein physician Bernard Kruger stepped away from roles at two concierge medical practices in March 2026; Sollis Health put him on board leave pending an external review.
AP reported some U.S. school districts paused or canceled Lifetouch sessions after viral posts made Epstein-related allegations.
AP reported Howard Lutnick acknowledged pre-government meetings with Epstein and that prior denials were inaccurate.
The Metropolitan Police arrested Peter Mandelson on February 23, 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office; he was later released under investigation.

Rep. Thomas Massie named 14 people on the House floor on August 31, 2026 whom he said should be investigated in connection with Epstein; the list is a floor allegation protected by the Speech or Debate Clause, not a charge, and those who have responded deny wrongdoing.
Judge Jesse Furman ruled on April 28, 2026 that fired Epstein and Maxwell prosecutor Maurene Comey's wrongful-termination suit can proceed in federal court.
Judge Paul Engelmayer denied Ghislaine Maxwell's pro se petition to vacate her conviction in an order made public on August 25, 2026.

Morgan McSweeney resigned as UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's chief of staff on February 8, 2026, taking responsibility for advising the appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador to the United States.

On July 21, 2026 Melania Trump moved for sanctions against author Michael Wolff after Judge Mary Kay Vyskocil dismissed his preemptive anti-SLAPP suit; the judge had cautioned against the motion on July 1, and no ruling had been reported as of September 24, 2026.
Mount Sinai Health System formed a board committee in late February 2026 to review its ties to Epstein; CNN reported in May that DOJ records show Epstein received preferential treatment there.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in late March 2026 that the league had found no personal-conduct violation by Steve Tisch, who is no longer a Giants owner after moving his stake into his children's trusts.

New Mexico's Department of Justice sent letters dated May 15, 2026 asking dozens of companies, including JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, Apple, Google, and several airlines, to preserve records tied to Epstein and Maxwell.

New Mexico's Survivors' Truth Commission said its interim report found evidence supporting reports of sexual abuse of at least five women and girls at Zorro Ranch between 1996 and 2012, and that its final report is due December 31, 2026.
Norwegian and French investigators formed a joint investigation team in late April 2026 covering the case against Mona Juul and Terje Rod-Larsen.
New York City reopened expired Gender-Motivated Violence Act claims when the City Council overrode a mayoral veto on January 29, 2026, creating a window that runs to about July 2027.
New York's Department of Health said on August 25, 2026 that allegations about doctors connected to Epstein were deeply troubling and warranted review; it did not name anyone.

Ohio State University's final report released June 23, 2026 found that Dr. Mark Landon was not aware of or involved in Epstein's crimes but likely violated university policy by not reporting or getting approval for outside consulting work.
On June 25, 2026, Judge Emmet Sullivan granted a preliminary injunction in Phang v. Blanche ordering DOJ to unredact disputed Epstein records or justify each redaction.
The House rejected a resolution to censure Del. Stacey Plaskett over texting Epstein during a February 2019 hearing by a vote of 209-214 on November 18, 2025.
Stacey Plaskett won the Democratic primary for governor of the U.S. Virgin Islands in August 2026 with about 48% of the vote.

On August 11, 2026, Judge Loretta Preska ruled the Epstein Files Transparency Act overrides earlier sealing orders, grand-jury secrecy, and Ghislaine Maxwell's privacy claims, clearing additional records for release.
A federal judge unsealed on May 6, 2026 a purported note that Nicholas Tartaglione says he found in July 2019; the court did not assess its authenticity.

The Institute for Primary Facts opened a reading room in New York displaying all 3,437 bound volumes of the released Epstein files from May 8 to May 21, 2026, and began a national tour in Dallas in September.

The book Regime Change by Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan reported that White House aides held Situation Room meetings in July 2025 on managing the Epstein files and that Vice President Vance proposed a Tucker Carlson interview of Ghislaine Maxwell.
Rome prosecutors opened a sexual-violence file against unknown persons concerning possible Italian links to Epstein and sent a letter rogatory to DOJ, as reported on September 5, 2026.

French model scout Daniel Siad, who was under French investigation over alleged recruitment for Epstein, was found dead at his home near Paris on July 20, 2026; the cause of death was under investigation.
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced his resignation on June 22, 2026 amid fallout over his appointment of Peter Mandelson as ambassador.

On September 16, 2026 Judge Emmet Sullivan ordered DOJ to give the court, for private review, redacted and unredacted handwritten notes from four 2019 FBI interviews of a woman identified as Jane Doe 4 by 11 a.m. on September 24, and declined to stay the order pending appeal.

On September 16, 2026, Judge Sullivan set a September 24 deadline for DOJ to produce disputed Epstein records or explain why his orders were not clear, and said a contempt finding would be premature at that juncture.
Epstein survivors and relatives attended President Trump's February 24, 2026 State of the Union address as guests of Democratic members of Congress.

Epstein survivors filed a proposed class action in the Northern District of California on March 26, 2026 against DOJ and Google, alleging the file releases exposed about 100 survivors' personal information and that Google kept republishing it.

On November 14, 2025 President Trump asked DOJ to investigate Epstein's ties to Bill Clinton, Larry Summers, Reid Hoffman, and JPMorgan Chase, and Attorney General Bondi assigned Jay Clayton to lead the inquiry; no charges or findings had been reported as of September 24, 2026.
On August 5, 2026 Downing Street said the UK government was not actively considering a public inquiry into Epstein, after the victims minister said Prime Minister Burnham was looking into one.
AP reported Casey Wasserman planned to sell his talent agency after publication of emails involving Ghislaine Maxwell.

At a September 1, 2026 meeting, his first since May 2025, Les Wexner said he would step down as chair of the Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center board while remaining a member; Ohio State had received more than 500 requests to remove his name from campus buildings.
Survivors' consolidated federal suit against Les Wexner and the Wexner Foundation was voluntarily dismissed without prejudice on September 1, 2026 amid a dispute over federal jurisdiction.
Judge Mary Kay Vyskocil dismissed Michael Wolff's preemptive suit against Melania Trump on May 22, 2026, calling it bad-faith forum shopping.

The Wall Street Journal reported on September 23, 2026 that federal prosecutors in Manhattan are investigating Epstein estate executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn; both deny wrongdoing and no charges have been filed.

Yale University barred computer science professor David Gelernter from teaching in February 2026 pending a conduct review of his emails with Epstein; in September 2026 Yale said the review was continuing and he would not teach in the fall.
